summary.text: A barometer is a scientific instrument for measuring air pressure.
Tracking how its readings change, known as pressure tendency, helps forecast short-term changes in the weather.
Evangelista Torricelli is usually credited with inventing it in 1643, after arguing that air has weight that holds up a column of liquid.

facts.label: Mercury column
facts.value: About 30 inches high, held up by air pressure

facts.label: Water column limit
facts.value: About 10.3 m in a sealed tube

facts.label: Close relative
facts.value: The pressure altimeter, essentially the same instrument

items.prompt: Torricelli switched from water to mercury in his tube experiment. What did that make possible?

options.label: Measuring temperature as well as pressure
Using a far shorter tube, under a metre
Making a perfect vacuum for the first time
Doing without a basin of liquid at all

items.explain: Mercury is about 14 times denser than water, so a tube of only 80 cm worked instead of one over 10 m.

items.prompt: Water in a tall sealed tube, standing in a basin, stops sinking at about 10 m. What did Torricelli say keeps the column up?

options.label: The pull of the empty space above it
Vapours rising from the water itself
Friction between water and the glass
The weight of air pressing on the basin

items.explain: Torricelli argued that air has weight, which pushes on the water in the basin rather than a vacuum sucking the water up.

items.prompt: Before Torricelli, what did Aristotelian thinkers, and even Galileo, assume about air?

options.label: That it weighed nothing at all
That it was heavier than water
That it was made mostly of fire
That it pressed down only when windy

items.explain: It was traditionally thought, especially by Aristotelians, that air had no weight, and even Galileo accepted this.

items.prompt: Pascal had a barometer carried up a mountain, the Puy de Dôme. If air has weight, what should its mercury column do on the way up?

options.label: Rise, as the air grows thinner
Stay put, since mercury is heavy
Drop, as pressure falls with height
Swing wildly with mountain winds

items.explain: If air has weight, pressure is lower higher up, so less pressure supports the mercury and the column should stand lower.

items.prompt: A pilot's pressure altimeter and a home barometer are essentially the same device. What differs?

options.label: The altimeter measures heat, not pressure
One infers height; the other tracks weather
The barometer works only at sea level
Only the altimeter has moving parts

items.explain: An altimeter compares pressure with expected values to estimate altitude, while a barometer stays at one altitude and tracks pressure changes from weather.

items.prompt: What is the pattern of change in barometer readings, called pressure tendency, mainly used for?

options.label: Predicting earthquakes before they strike
Measuring how humid the air is
Tracking climate over many decades
Forecasting short-term weather changes

items.explain: Pressure tendency, taken from barometer readings, can forecast short-term changes in the weather.
